verdict.headline: Palantir's 149% commercial surge and Dow record reframe the AI-spending thesis
verdict.label: BUY — Dow 53,178 record; SPX 7,600 (+1.48%); Nasdaq 25,914 (+2.13%); PLTR $127 day close → $142 AH (+11.8%); Q2 $1.94B (+93% YoY), US commercial +149%; ISM 55.6% (4-yr high); 30Y 5.20%, September hike 64.5% (below 70% gate); WTI $79.62 (−5.97%); 2-of-6 breaches; AMD earnings AH Tuesday
verdict.rationale_short: Today's session validated and exceeded the morning's constructive read. PLTR's AH print answered the morning's central uncertainty directly: US commercial revenue accelerated to 149% YoY — faster than the DoD government line — meaning the AI platform adoption thesis is enterprise-broad, not defense-urgency-driven. FY26 guidance was raised to $8.15B vs. the $7.65B prior consensus. ISM Manufacturing printed at 55.6% (4-year high), above the 54.0 expected, with prices paid at 71.1% — a hawkish data print — but September hike held at 64.5%, below the 70% formal trigger, as oil deflation continued to dominate the rate market. WTI dropped nearly 6% to $79.62 after Trump announced renewed Iran peace talks. The regime breach count is 2 of 6: 30Y yield at 5.20% above 5.00%, and WTI at $79.62 barely above the $79 breach threshold. AMD (+12.7% to $484.64) front-ran the PLTR read-through ahead of its own AH print Tuesday. Conviction is medium, not high: AMD's binary still looms, ISM prices-paid printed hotter than expected, and the $79 WTI breach is within $0.62 of clearing. The read changes if SPX closes below 7,380 or if WTI re-breaches $85 on a ceasefire reversal.

watchlist_mentions.note: ~$127 day close, $142 AH (+11.8%). Q2 revenue $1.94B (+93% YoY) vs. $1.81B consensus. US commercial +149% YoY (vs. +98% expected) — the commercial acceleration is the structural shift from a DoD-urgency story to a broad enterprise-AI story. FY26 guidance raised to $8.15B (+82% YoY) vs. $7.65B prior consensus. Rule of 40 at 155%. The morning's concern that Iran de-escalation would unwind government revenue was answered: DoD revenue also beat, but commercial grew faster.

$484.64 (+12.7% on the day), ahead of AH Tuesday. PLTR's 149% commercial beat is a strong read-through for AI platform spending into AMD's MI350/Helios cycle. Additional context: AMD's $5B Anthropic deal (announced July 22) — Anthropic purchasing up to 2GW of MI450 chips on AMD's Helios rack-scale system, first GW deploying H1 2027 — makes AMD-specific AI adoption a direct Q2 focus. Consensus: $11.31B revenue (+47% YoY), $1.61 EPS, data-center >$6B (95% Polymarket). Options pricing 10% swing from $484. The +12.7% pre-earnings move has pre-loaded the bull case; in-line data-center revenue risks a sell-the-news reversal from an elevated base. Bull trigger: data-center above $7B AND confirmed Helios/MI450 ramp timeline for H1 2027.

dont_buy.reason: AMD closed +12.7% at $484.64 ahead of AH earnings Tuesday. The PLTR read-through is fully priced; an inline or slight data-center beat from a pre-elevated base risks a sell-the-news move. The Anthropic deal context raises the bar further — market now expects Helios/MI450 ramp specifics to accompany the revenue print. The setup demands data-center above $6B AND MI450 ramp timeline confirmation to justify the pre-earnings bid.
dont_buy.better_entry: Post-print, after confirming data-center above $6B and MI450/Helios ramp timeline; $440-450 on a revenue in-line result would represent a reset to prior support.

trade_setups.thesis: AMD reports AH Tuesday with revenue consensus $11.31B (+47% YoY), data-center >$6B (95% Polymarket probability), and options pricing a 10% swing from $484. The stock closed +12.7% today on PLTR read-through — the AI spend cycle is confirmed, but the bar entering Tuesday's print is now higher. The AMD-Anthropic $5B deal (July 22) means Wall Street expects Helios rack-scale commentary and MI450 deployment timelines alongside the revenue line. The binary: data-center above $7B and MI450 ramp confirmed for H1 2027 is the double-confirmation leg. Data-center inline at $6B or below, or any AMZN custom-silicon displacement commentary, compresses the multiple from the pre-loaded base.
trade_setups.entry: Watch AH print: >$7B data-center with ramp confirmation, $540+ opens as the next target from $484; data-center $5.5B or below, $440-450 is near-term reset.
trade_setups.invalidation: Data-center revenue misses $5.5B or management signals Helios rack-scale delays beyond H1 2027.

trade_setups.thesis: WTI closed at $79.62 today — $0.62 above the $79 formal breach threshold — after a 5.97% drop on Iran peace talk resumption. A single sustained close below $79 reduces the breach count from 2-of-6 to 1-of-6 (30Y only), which would be the most constructive regime position in months. What reverses it: any IRGC military action or Trump rhetoric re-escalating the Hormuz risk premium. Brent $83.82 is now $1.18 below the $85 breach threshold — a co-clear is achievable in two more sessions of Iran diplomacy.
trade_setups.entry: Not a position; a regime threshold to monitor at each day's close. Two consecutive closes below $79 formally clear this breach indicator.
trade_setups.invalidation: WTI close above $82 on re-escalation restores both oil-side breaches simultaneously.

trade_setups.asset: July NFP August 7 — September hike binary
trade_setups.thesis: September hike has moved from 82.4% (July 31) to 64.5% (August 3), below the 70% formal trigger, on oil deflation. Friday NFP (consensus +91K, prior 147K) determines whether that improvement holds. Above 130K: September hike rebounds toward 70%+, re-triggers the formal breach, 30Y extends toward 5.25-5.30%, and the two oil-cleared breaches stand alone. Below 80K: September falls below 55%, 30Y can approach the 5.00% clearing threshold, and breach count has a path to 1-of-6. The 80K-130K range keeps September in neutral territory (55-70%).
trade_setups.entry: Watch September hike probability in CME FedWatch within 30 minutes of the 8:30 AM ET print. 30Y yield direction is the real-time regime signal.
trade_setups.invalidation: Sub-80K print with cooling average hourly earnings clears the 30Y breach zone on a lagged basis.

bear_case: ISM at 55.6% with prices paid 71.1% and managers describing inflation as 'worse than pandemic era' is not a disinflationary print — it is the strongest manufacturing output in four years with elevated cost pressures. Oil deflation carried the rate market today, but the Brent ceasefire has collapsed twice before in 2026 (both times rebounding above $100). If Brent reverses above $85 and Friday NFP prints above 130K, September hike surges back through 70% and the two cleared breaches restore immediately. PLTR at $142 AH trades at approximately 83x forward sales — the 149% US commercial growth must sustain to justify that multiple, and a deceleration to 100% in Q3 at this valuation would compress the stock without the DoD urgency as a floor. AMD's +12.7% pre-earnings move means the AI-spend thesis is fully priced ahead of the print; the AMD-Anthropic deal raises the bar further — the market now needs Helios ramp confirmation, not just a revenue beat. BTC at $63,455 (9:13pm ET) holds Gate 2 with a $1,455 buffer, but Friday NFP remains the next macro stress event. The read does not hold if SPX closes below 7,380.
